results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** AC, the one fixed finite-type surface and generating loop system, the common positive graph expansion, and the varying covers.

[A1] Full choice is [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[F1] Quadratic pushforward is normally convergent on compact subsets and has norm at most one for any connected cover of a finite-type surface. [[thm-nonamenable-coverings-contract-integrable-quadratic-differentials]]

[F2] Cauchy's formula gives the local holomorphic mean-value bound; Laurent coefficients have the circle formula; locally bounded holomorphic families have locally uniformly convergent subsequences. [[thm-cauchy-integral-formula-circle]], [[thm-laurent-expansion-annulus]], [[thm-montel-theorem-for-holomorphic-functions]]



1.1 If $Q(X)=0$, take $c=0$. Otherwise suppose no common $c<1$ exists. Choose covers $p_n:Y_n\to X$ with the common expansion and $q_n\in Q(Y_n)$ such that $\|q_n\|_1=1$ and $\|\Theta_{p_n}q_n\|_1\to1$. The unit ball of $Q(X)$ is compact in $L^1$. Here is the needed finite-type argument. At a puncture an integrable coefficient $f$ has no Laurent terms of degree at most $-2$: its circle means $M(r)$ satisfy $\int rM(r)dr<\infty$, so along some $r_j\downarrow0$ one has $r_j^2M(r_j)\to0$, and the coefficient bound $|a_{-m}|\le r_j^mM(r_j)$ kills every $m\ge2$. On a fixed surrounding circle the mean-value bound uniformly bounds unit-norm coefficients, hence bounds the possible simple-pole coefficient and the holomorphic remainder on a smaller disc. Thus their puncture tails have uniformly vanishing $L^1$ mass, bounded by $C(r+r^2)$. On the remaining compact region [F2] gives locally uniform subsequence compactness, and the tail bound upgrades it to $L^1$ compactness. Therefore pass to $\Theta_{p_n}q_n\to\psi$ in $L^1(X)$ with $\|\psi\|_1=1$. Put $\mu=\overline\psi/|\psi|$ off its zeros and zero at its zeros. Then the nonnegative inefficiency integrals satisfy $$I_n=\int_{Y_n}(|q_n|-\operatorname{Re}(q_np_n^*\mu))=1-\operatorname{Re}\int_X(\Theta_{p_n}q_n)\mu\longrightarrow0.$$ The norm and convergence facts use only the one fixed surface, although the domains vary. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 We require a uniform local rigidity fact, independent of the covering. If $h$ is holomorphic on a Euclidean disc of area $A$, $\int|h|=1$ and $\operatorname{Re}\int h\ge1-\epsilon$, then $\|h-1/A\|_1\to0$ as $\epsilon\to0$. Reduce to the unit disc by scaling. The bound $\int|\operatorname{Im}h|\le\sqrt{2\epsilon}$ follows from $|\operatorname{Im}h|^2\le2|h|(|h|-\operatorname{Re}h)$ and Cauchy–Schwarz. The mean-value bound and Montel in [F2] show any subsequential local limit is a real constant, necessarily $1/\pi$ by its mean at zero. On a radius-$r$ subdisc its absolute mass tends to $r^2$, so the remaining mass tends to $1-r^2$. Split the $L^1$ error into these two regions and let $r\uparrow1$. If no uniform modulus existed, a sequence with $\epsilon\to0$ and errors bounded below would contradict this argument. This proves the claimed qualitative modulus. [F2, construct, algebra]

2.1 Represent the fixed generating loops away from the discrete zeros of $\psi$, without changing their based homotopy classes (moving the basepoint by a fixed connecting path if necessary changes the monodromy graphs only by a fiber relabeling). Cover their union by a connected finite net of equal-radius flat discs $E_1,\ldots,E_J$ for $\psi=dw^2$. The radii are less than one quarter of the minimum flat coordinate radius on a compact neighborhood of the loops. Every nonempty pairwise overlap is therefore a connected Euclidean lens; the finite net carries the generating loops. Let $A$ be the common disc area and $a>0$ the smallest lens area divided by $A$. For each cover its lifted intersection graph has degree at most $J-1$, since connected base overlaps identify at most one lift of a neighboring disc. It has an expansion lower bound $\gamma_0>0$ independent of $n$. Explicitly choose an anchor disc, let $C$ bound lengths of fixed base disc chains connecting every disc type to the anchor, let $L$ bound chains for the supplied generators, and put $D=\max(2,J)$. For a finite lifted vertex set $V$, at least $|V|/D^{C+1}$ anchor vertices lie within distance $C$ of it. Their monodromy border has size at least $\gamma|V|/D^{C+1}$, and each such outside anchor lies within $L+C$ edges of $b(V)$: concatenate a path from $V$ to its inside neighboring anchor with the generator chain and take its first exit from $V$. Bounded degree gives $\gamma_0=\gamma D^{-(L+2C+3)}$ as a valid common lower bound. All these constants depend only on the one net and the supplied common expansion. [given, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 On a lifted flat disc $E$ in $Y_n$ write $m_n(E)=\int_E|q_n|$ and $i_n(E)=m_n(E)^{-1}\int_E(|q_n|-\operatorname{Re}(q_np_n^*\mu))$. Its mass is positive by holomorphic uniqueness on connected $Y_n$. Step 1.2 says that for $i_n(E)<\epsilon$ the differential $q_n$ differs in $L^1(E)$ from $(m_n(E)/A)p_n^*\psi$ by at most $\eta m_n(E)$, where $\eta\to0$ uniformly with $\epsilon$. Integrating these errors on an overlap shows that two neighboring efficient discs have mass ratios at least $\lambda=(a-\eta)/(a+\eta)$ in either direction; a neighbor of one efficient disc has mass at least $(a-\eta)$ times its mass even if that neighbor is inefficient. Fix $\eta<a/2$ so small that $\lambda^{-1}-1<\gamma_0/2$, and choose one $\epsilon>0$ giving this modulus. These constants are uniform in $n$ and in the covering. [step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 We give the weighted graph estimate so its uniformity is explicit. For an efficient vertex set $V$ with positive summable weights $m$ and neighboring ratios at least $\lambda$, put $F(w)=\sup_{v\in V,v\sim w}m(v)$ for $w\notin V$. Apply expansion to the finite superlevel sets $\{v\in V:m(v)>t\}$ and integrate in $t$. Outside vertices contribute at most $F(w)$. An inside vertex of mass $m(v)$ contributes to the integrated border only for $m(v)\le t<\lambda^{-1}m(v)$, at most $(\lambda^{-1}-1)m(v)$. Hence $$\sum_{w\notin V}F(w)\ge(\gamma_0-(\lambda^{-1}-1))\sum_{v\in V}m(v)\ge\frac{\gamma_0}{2}\sum_{v\in V}m(v).$$ For the efficient discs $V_n$ of step 3.1, every outside neighbor has mass at least $(a-\eta)F(w)$. Thus the total inefficient mass is at least $c_0=(a-\eta)\gamma_0/2$ times the efficient mass, uniformly. Also $\epsilon$ times the inefficient mass is at most $JI_n$, because every point occurs in at most $J$ lifted discs. Since $I_n\to0$, both masses tend to zero. Their sum, however, is at least $$\int_{p_n^{-1}(\cup E_j)}|q_n|\ge\int_{\cup E_j}|\Theta_{p_n}q_n|\longrightarrow\int_{\cup E_j}|\psi|>0,$$ a contradiction. All weighted sums are summable by the multiplicity bound; layer-cake interchange is of nonnegative terms. This proves the one uniform $c<1$, with no compactness assumption on the varying covers themselves. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For a countable family $p_j:Y_j\to X$ and differentials with $\sum_j\|q_j\|_1<\infty$, the series $\sum_j\Theta_{p_j}q_j$ is absolutely convergent in $L^1$ and normally convergent on compact subsets by the mean-value bound [F2]. Its limit is holomorphic and integrable, and its norm is at most $\sum_jc\|q_j\|_1$. Thus the sum operator is defined and has norm at most the same $c$. Every constant in the contradiction proof was chosen after fixing the limiting unit differential on the one fixed $X$, the one generating system and the common $\gamma$; no cover-dependent constant entered. No conclusion about degenerating complex structures was used. [F1, F2, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎



The existing entire strict-cover-pushforward proof and all its actual Cauchy, Laurent and Montel supplier proofs were read in full. The complete cached McMullen amenability article was previously read, all34 pages including the appendix and references, SHA256 9b84fd64445941d2d64e1ca95cf9553ed35aa975ce71199a0a65e7636dde38fd. The varying-cover argument is written out rather than inferring a uniform bound from pointwise strictness.

This supplies the common-cover contraction needed for countably many conformal-boundary spots at a fixed marked surface. Identifying the actual spot covering family, proving its common expansion from topology, identifying the skinning coderivative, and controlling degeneration in moduli remain distinct obligations. It does not replace those operations or complete the original hyperbolization proof.
